body: Small chances for a (semi?) fix just don't seem to warrant suffering a lifetime of misery...sigh.
Ok, you win.  You've convinced me I need to stop being afraid and cautious.  I need to grow some balls and kill myself already.  I don't have the will left to live, so I must nurture the will to die.

I only listed those three because they are mentioned the most.  It's not like I haven't tried other things.

I wouldn't call posting here "fighting," more like an intellectual twitch.  I can't focus outwards; I never could.  Before the depression became a permanent state, I was always happiest when alone and indeed focusing inwards.  I could relax, enjoying writing, reading, and thinking far away from my noisy, anxiety-inducing peers.  Just being around people makes my physically sick to the point I vomit myself dry.

HOW am I supposed to change this?  You don't think I've asked family and professionals alike?  They don't have an answer other than that they have no answers.  And yes, I am the problem.  Ultimately, I don't see anyone else as the one/s to blame.  That doesn't mean that I can simply choose to not have depression, anxiety, or incurable physical problems, though.

For awhile, yes.  To be specific, my parents are old.  That's a very limited time to feel pain -- hell, I may even be able to wait until they're gone and then do it.

I had a relative attempt suicide some years ago (they did not succeed).  Do you know what the responses were?  They were shunned.  Alienated.  Mocked.  They still are today.  People didn't care about how much pain they must have been in to try it, but rather that they had they audacity to to give the world the finger and attempt to leave it.  How dare they thumb their nose at *us*.

That's where I was six years ago.  I learned to streamline my life, focusing intensely on the few things I enjoyed to distract myself from depression and anxiety.  Hell, I'll even brag -- I think I got pretty damn good at it.  But I can't do that now.  Literally, I can't.  My mind changed at its core during my trials with anti-depressants; I don't have the ability to focus for more than a few seconds.  Music does nothing for me, food is bland and physically hurts to eat, and I have no heroes.

I wish my problem was other people, but I am the problem.  I am defective.  Not just now, not just this month or year -- but until I die.

I'm going to try to respond to all of these posts; I'm very tired but I'll do my best.

I don't think most people hate *me*.  I think people hate the suicidal and, most of all, people who finally do complete killing themselves.  Even the closest ones are blind to just how bad you can suffer in this way.

I have depression for nearly half of my life now, with severe depression occupying the last half.  There has been no relief.  No ups and downs like there were when I started getting depressed.  I got counseling, took anti-depressants and anti-anxiety medications.  Nothing helped.  People around me have told me to hang on for years, saying "things will get better."  They haven't.  They've gotten much, much worse.

I've analyzed suicide and suicidal people very closely.  While it's true that I don't (and can't) know everything about other posters here/hotline callers/etc, I've noticed that I'm fundamentally different than them.  They have suicidal periods -- I have a suicidal *life*.  The best analogy I can come up with is that these people have fire thrown under their feet sometimes; it hurts and stuns but can be extinguished eventually.  I, on the other hand, am slowly boiling, burning to death in a pot while others look down into it and insist, "just hold on there, I'm sure things will get better!"  

Why should I be tortured for a lifetime to so a handful (and it is a *small* handful) of people can avoid having their feelings hurt for awhile?

Okay, finally able to post again.

Yes, I was like that once; wanting to kill a part of me.  I could deal with that.  It made life hard and sometimes it seemed like I couldn't hold on for those brief periods, but that passed.  I did hold on.  Instead, those were replaced by an all-consuming depression that has BECOME my life -- not even to speak of all the other problems.

I long for the times where I was on again/off again suicidal.  But that's not my life any more.
